seeds.text: Self-abandonment is the quiet betrayal no one sees. Most of it happens in micro-moments — the small moment you don't take your own side.
There are no bad parts. Only parts carrying burdens they were never meant to hold. Healing is unburdening, not eliminating.
You are the sky. Everything else is weather. Identifying with the storm is what makes it permanent.
You don't have a dark side. You have an unmet one. What looks like darkness is usually a part nobody has ever been kind to.
You don't become whole by imagining figures of light. You become whole by making the darkness conscious — that's where the energy is.

slides.text: These aren't bad parts. They are parts carrying burdens they were never meant to hold.

slides.text: Ignoring them is a micro-betrayal. It's how self-abandonment quietly begins.
slides.composition: A distant silhouette of a person standing at a glowing, ornate archway, but their back is turned, walking away from the light.

slides.text: Wholeness isn't imagining light. It's making these unloved parts conscious. That's where the energy is.
slides.composition: An abstract cosmic field with a central vortex of deep blues and purples, from which brilliant golden sparks are emerging and expanding.

slides.text: You don't fix them. You turn towards them, ask what they need, and let them be seen.
slides.composition: Overhead view of two chrome hands, one slightly cupped, reaching towards a small, quiet pool of reflective, liquid silver.

slides.text: This quiet turning is the deepest kind of kindness you can offer yourself.
slides.composition: A single, soft-focus prismatic lens flare expands gently across a textured pastel gradient, embodying peace and gentle expansion.

caption:
We're so quick to call parts of ourselves "dark" or "bad." But what if they're just... lonely? Unmet? This is where the real work (and healing) begins. Sending you warmth.
